main_strengths: The benchmark is fixed and the school reasoning is real. 19/19 compare M2 with ~2% trend real growth plus the 2% target (about 4%); 0/19 use one quarter's GDP print as the benchmark, and 6 say outright that one GDP quarter is not a trend. The natural rate now appears in 7/19 (0/17 in v2). Several items use the right Monetarist tool for the event: sterilized vs unsterilized intervention (m0005), the deposit multiplier and equity raising vs asset shrinkage (m0006), base vs broad money with fiscal transfers as what made 2020 inflationary (m0007), the stablecoin as inside money whose loss a money rule should offset (m0010), a pegged EM importing US money (m0016), RRR cuts replacing maturing PBoC lending (m0018), and mortgage relief working on velocity and precautionary demand (m0017). No Keynesian or Austrian logic.

The grounding mechanics are clean. Tool results are now code-generated and consistent. No trajectory cites an episode id or indicator value the tools did not return (checked automatically; the unrequested 2y in m0015 can be derived from the 10y and the spread), and every number matches the tool output or the event. 19/19 say where each analog fits and where it does not: m0013 picks the 2003 threat analog over 1973, m0014 separates Red Sea 2023 from Suez 2021 by the money backdrop, and m0016 admits the episodes record no US outcome. Velocity is inferred from the data in 5/19 (m0007, m0008, m0010, m0017, m0018). Weakest-link lines are specific and honest.

Signals now weigh the scenario distribution. Most reasons cite combined weights ('S1 and S3 together at 0.72', 'only S3 at 0.18 argues the other way'). Reasons resting on S1 alone fell to about 9 of 114 lines (97/102 in v2). Directions follow the event type: easing and positive events get credit LONG or NEUTRAL and equities NEUTRAL or LONG (m0000, m0002, m0007, m0017). Oil goes NEUTRAL when the event does not touch it (m0007, m0009, m0010, m0014, m0017). Gold is SHORT in 3/19 (0/17 before) under weak money or high real yields, and bonds flip SHORT in high-M2 backdrops.

The 'no bp' disclaimer is gone (0/19), and so is the exact 0.55/0.25/0.20 tuple (0/19). Sizing is better: 'several banks' raising capital is read as a recapitalisation, not a run (m0006); a blockade risk is kept apart from a blockade (m0013); a stablecoin float is small next to M2 (m0010); 500bn is small next to the BoJ balance sheet, with the missing currency noted (m0007); and a foreign shutdown gets equities NEUTRAL instead of v2's full risk-off set (m0015). m0017, m0009 and m0014 are near-exemplary.
main_problems: A new prompt echo appears in 19/19: an event-vs-data weighing sentence ('I weigh the event (more)' verbatim in 17, variants in m0014 and m0015). Only m0002's marks a real contradiction (the event says inflation is 2pp above target, CPI is 1.6%). m0009, m0013 and m0014 use it sensibly to weigh two forces. The rest treat a pre-event curve, GDP or CPI level as contradicting the event. In m0007, m0011, m0016 and m0018 the sentence contradicts the item's own conclusion, and m0010 makes it a [Proof] step.

Pre-event values are read as outcomes of the event. m0000 treats the 6.02% 10y and +71bp 2s10s as 'the market's verdict' on the cut (chain and Proof). m0002 calls 1.75% the policy rate 'after a 50bp cut'. m0016 says the -60bp inversion prices the response to the default. m0001 makes the -1.0% GDP print the PMI's consequence. m0018 asserts 'the Fed must tighten' while the 2y implied by the returned 10y and spread (1.30%) prices cuts.

One stock mechanism still dominates. 'Relative-price shock, inflation only if money accommodates' appears in 19/19, up to 9 times per item. The backdrop oil level is woven into the chain or scenarios of 7 events that are not about oil (m0000, m0001, m0002, m0003, m0006, m0010, m0017); m0002 calls $80 oil a shock. The phrase is misapplied to an unemployment print (m0011), a valuation writedown (m0004, garbled) and an RRR cut (m0018). Velocity is misread in 3 items: m0000 asserts it is stable; m0011 reads 12.9% M2 against ~2.3% nominal growth as 'spending arriving in prices'; m0015 denies a velocity offset while nominal GDP outruns M2. m0013 ignores it.

Probabilities and confidence are templated in a new way. S1 = 0.45 in 9/19, and three tuples repeat across 7 items ((0.45, 0.30, 0.25) x3; (0.45, 0.25, 0.20, 0.10) x2; (0.45, 0.30, 0.15, 0.10) x2). S1 is the modal scenario in 17/19. 'Confidence: moderate' appears in 19/19, never high or low, even for m0011's false premise. About 11/19 have two or more scenarios with identical growth/inflation labels. Four foreign events never say whose growth or inflation (m0003, m0007, m0015, m0018).

Credit SHORT 14/19. The event justifies it in 8 (m0001 PMI collapse, m0003 developer default, m0004 CRE writedown, m0006 bank CRE losses, m0008 coup, m0011 unemployment jump, m0013 blockade risk, m0016 EM default). It is weak in 3: m0010's reserve pool is bills, repo and CP; m0014 cites a margin channel while equities stay NEUTRAL; m0019 rests on a 0.25 scenario for a shock the item calls small. It is a default or backdrop call in 3: m0005 is a sterilized intervention that changes nothing, m0015 rests on S4 = 0.10, and m0018 is an easing. Wide spreads are read as 'little cushion' (m0003, m0018). The 5 non-SHORT credit calls all go to easing or positive events. Gold LONG 10/19 is mostly backed by high M2 or negative real rates. But in m0016 and m0019 it is a backdrop call unrelated to the event (m0019's highest conviction), m0007's rests on a 0.15 scenario and m0002's on S1 alone. Equities SHORT with gold LONG occurs in 4 items (m0001, m0008, m0011, m0019) and is a clear default only in m0019. Signals still follow S1 alone or map scenarios wrongly in m0002 (bonds, USD, gold), m0011 (bonds SHORT 4), m0016 (credit 'worst in S3', oil 'except S4'), m0013 (oil vs S2) and m0007 (dollar against its own chain).

Some factual and causal errors would be learned by a student. m0011 calls a 0.3pp monthly unemployment rise 'a typical monthly move' and builds the analysis on that. m0019 puts a Latin American tariff's price effect into US prices; it raises Latin American import prices, and for the US it is lost export demand. m0005 says Plaza's dollar fall did not cause inflation 'because money growth was not accommodated', but US M2 grew ~9% and M1 at double digits in 1985-86. m0011 says 2019's easing came with no money acceleration (M2 went from ~4% to ~6.7%); m0000 relies on the same premise. m0003 says US nominal income fell 'for years' after 2006 as money failed to accommodate (M2 +9-10% in 2008). m0009 says 2022 was 'then accommodated'. m0010 treats forced T-bill sales as bullish for the front end.

Format and input gaps. 6/19 [Proof] blocks exceed 7 lines (m0005 has 9; m0006, m0007, m0010, m0016 and m0018 have 8), and m0008 drops the [ ] refs. The stand-in episode table has no money-substitute runs, PBoC RRR cuts or mortgage-relief programmes, so m0010 takes Archegos as its base rate and m0017 calls the Greek bailout a 'housing/debt programme'. The backdrop generator still produces impossible mixes (0.9% CPI with $126 oil and a 6.02% 10y; a 0.3% 10y with 4.9% CPI) and contradicts levels the event states (m0002). It has no lagged series, so lags are only asserted and nearly every weakest link says one M2 print cannot show direction.
suggested_prompt_or_template_changes: Replace the rule behind 'I weigh the event' (19/19) with: 'Returned indicators are pre-event. Mention a contradiction only when the event text states a level the data contradict (e.g. inflation 2pp above target vs CPI 1.6%). A shock that will move a variable from its pre-event level is not a contradiction. Never read a returned yield, spread, rate or GDP print as the market's or the economy's response to the event.' Validator: count 'weigh(t) the event' and reject a batch above ~20%.

Add a velocity step to the school diagnosis: 'Before calling velocity stable or saying money is arriving in prices, compute implied velocity growth = CPI y/y + real growth - M2 y/y, and say which real-growth figure you used.' State the benchmark as a band (about 3.5-4.5% for 2% trend + 2% target) so readings of 3.0-4.6% do not get binary 'starving' or 'excessive' verdicts.

Restrict the stock mechanism: 'Use the supply-shock/accommodation argument only for supply shocks. Do not treat the backdrop oil level as a live shock unless the event concerns energy.' Add per-category hints. Labour: the natural rate, and a monthly change of 0.2pp or more is statistically significant. Banking: deposit multiplier and money demand. FX: sterilization; a central bank selling its own currency cannot run out of ammunition. Tariffs: who levies them and where the price effect lands. RRR: multiplier vs base, MLF replacement. Runs on private money: money substitutes and the rule-consistent offset.

Scenarios: 'No default S1; probabilities come from this event and backdrop. Scenarios must differ in growth or inflation direction. For a foreign event, label growth and inflation by economy.' collect() should report the S1 histogram, repeated tuples (S1 = 0.45 in 9/19; three tuples repeat across 7 items) and the share of identical labels.

Confidence: 'high when the data, analogs and mechanism agree; low when the decisive link is unobserved or the analogs fit poorly.' The batch report should warn when one level exceeds ~70% (moderate is 19/19 here).

Signals: 'A signal that rests on a scenario below 0.25 gets NEUTRAL or conviction 1. Signals express the event's marginal effect; a call driven only by the backdrop must say so and carry conviction 2 or less. Wide spreads mean more is priced in, not less cushion.' The batch report should warn when an asset's modal direction exceeds ~65% (credit SHORT is 14/19).
Proof validator: enforce 4-7 lines of the form '- Lk [ref]:' (6/19 exceed; m0008 drops the brackets), and reject a Proof line that only says how the event was weighed against the data.

Episode table: add money-substitute runs (Reserve Primary 2008, Terra 2022, USDC/SVB 2023), PBoC RRR cuts (2015, 2018, 2019), mortgage relief (HOLC 1933, HAMP 2009) and FX interventions by a central bank selling its own currency (SNB 2011 floor). Store each episode's money-growth context in the table so claims about money growth in an analog come from the tool, not from memory. That would have prevented the Plaza, 2019, 2006-07 and 2022 errors.

Backdrop generator: condition on levels the event states (T01-05); tie the 2y and 10y to inflation and the policy rate, and oil to CPI; add 'M2 growth y/y 12 months earlier', 'nominal GDP y/y' and 'real GDP 4-quarter average' so lags and velocity can be shown from data. Templates: name the commodity in T05-04, give currency and period in T01-04 (e.g. 500bn yen per month), and use a spending freeze in T02-06 for economies without shutdowns.

Before scaling: keep m0017, m0009, m0014, m0013, m0008 and m0006 as exemplars once the weighing sentence is removed. Regenerate m0011 (false 0.3pp premise), m0019 (tariff incidence) and m0018 (assumed Fed tightening, default credit SHORT). Fix m0005 (Plaza), m0002 (post-cut misread), m0016 (scenario mapping) and m0000 (curve read as reaction).
